To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the regulatory requirement of patient-specific prescriptions for intravitreal bevacizumab (IVB) resulted in a decrease in the number of patients treated with IVB.

the implementation of a regulatory requirement for patient-specific prescriptions for off-label medications was associated with a significant decrease in the use of intravitreal bevacizumab, a decrease that persisted for at least 6 months after implementation.

the implementation of a regulatory requirement to write patient-specific prescriptions for off-label medications was associated with a decrease in the number of patients receiving intravitreal bevacizumab for age-related macular degeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the drug bevacizumab for the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
the use of intravitreal bevacizumab in patients with diabetic retinopathy.
the effect of the regulatory requirement for patient-specific prescriptions for off-label medications on the use of intravitreal bevacizumab (Avastin) for treatment of retinal vascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of the present study indicate that the use of intravitreal bevacizumab in patients with DME was significantly reduced after the introduction of a regulatory requirement for a patient-specific prescription.
the use of intravitreal bevacizumab in the treatment of diabetic macular edema is not supported by the available data and that the use of this drug is not recommended.

, the results of this study suggest that the requirement for a specific prescription for off-label medications may not be a significant factor in the use of intravitreal bevacizumab in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of intravitreal bevacizumab for treatment of retinal vascular disorders in the United States is decreasing, and this trend is likely related to the requirement for patient-specific prescriptions for off-label use.
the effect of regulatory requirement for patient-specific prescriptions for off-label medications on the use of intravitreal bevacizumab is not clear.

there is a significant increase in the use of bevacizumab after the implementation of the regulatory requirement for patient-specific prescriptions, but the effect is not significant in the use of ranibizumab.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the FDA’s recent requirement for patient-specific prescriptions for intravitreal bevacizumab (Avastin) for off-label use in ophthalmology has not been met with the intended effect of decreasing use of this agent.

regulatory requirements for patient-specific prescriptions for off-label medications are not associated with reduced use of intravitreal bevacizumab for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration.
the FDA's requirement for prescribers to obtain an individual patient-specific prescription for off-label medications may have unintended negative effects on the use of such treatments.
